title: Loops in Omega: while with a bound, for with a count
keywords: how do I write a loop
summary: Asked how to write a loop in Omega? There are two shapes: while COND bound N ... end, and for i T K ... end, plus break and continue. Drake made every loop finite: bound N (1..999999, default 1000000) is a promise, and one pass more stops the program with trap 4, exit 104. I'll show you how to choose N from a short proof in a note, and what the trap looks like when the proof is wrong.
goal: Write bounded while loops, counted for loops, break and continue, and recognise trap 4.
key_steps: Write while COND bound N with N from a proof in a note
Use for i T K for a counted loop (i = 0..K-1)
Use break to leave and continue to skip to the next pass
Build a do-while as while true bound N with a break at the end
Read exit 104 as a loop that ran past its bound, and error 8 as a bound outside 1..999999

example.code:
note loops.om: while with a bound, for with a count, break, and a do-while shape
fn gcd a uint b uint to uint
note Euclid: b falls every pass; 64 passes is far more than 32-bit inputs need
while ne b 0 bound 64
t = rem a b
a = b
b = t
end
ret a
end
fn putnum v ulong to long
note write v in decimal and a newline. A ulong has at most 20 digits, so bound 20 is proved
d = new uchar 21 0
o = new uchar 21 0
n = ulong 0
x = v
while true bound 20
put d n uchar add rem x 10 48
n = add n 1
x = div x 10
if eq x 0
break
end
end
for i ulong n
put o i get d sub sub n i 1
end
put o n 10
w = write 1 o 0 add n 1
ret w
end
fn main to int
g = gcd 1071 462
w = putnum ulong g
s = ulong 0
for i ulong 10
s = add s i
end
w = putnum s
f = ulong 0
for i ulong 100
if gt mul i i 3000
f = i
break
end
end
w = putnum f
ret 0
end

common_mistake: Choosing a bound by feel or making it huge so the trap never fires. Write the termination argument in a note and choose N from it; when trap 4 (exit 104) fires, the proof was wrong, not the bound too small. Also: and/or evaluate both sides, so guard a get with an outer if, not with and.
